title: Windowed debit double-count from shard epoch overlap causing per-route quota spikes
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Intermittent double-debits observed on per-route quota counters when shard lease handoffs occur during a rolling merge. Affected flows see short spikes of quota consumption (typically 1-3 seconds) where identical requests are charged twice for the same token window.

Why it matters: Double-charging inflates usage for customers, can trigger unplanned rate-limits and quota exhaustion, and causes billing/accounting mismatches between realtime meter outputs and downstream billing aggregation. This first surfaced in customer incidents where production traffic patterns include heavy route aliasing and autoscaler-driven shard rebalancing.

Root cause hypothesis: The windowed-debit engine uses an epoch id to determine whether a calculated debit belongs to the current shard ownership window. During lease handoff we observed an epoch overlap race: the old shard emits a debit with epoch N and the new shard also emits a debit for the same logical request with epoch N+1 before the router's in-flight dedupe filter observes the ownership transfer. Because per-route keys are normalized at routing time (route alias -> canonical route) and that normalization happens slightly after shard selection in the hot path, the dedupe layer does not consistently match the two events, allowing both debits to be applied.

Contributing factors observed: 1) Router normalization happening after shard selection (timing window). 2) Deduplication window keyed by (route, request-id) with a TTL that was set too short relative to the observed handoff latency. 3) Shard handoff emits both a final reconciliation debit and a first-of-new-epoch synthetic debit for safety; those two combined without a strong-idempotency check cause double-apply.

Proposed fix: Add a stable, route-normalized dedupe key upstream of shard selection so both pre- and post-handoff events map to the same dedupe bucket. Extend dedupe TTL for lease-handoff events to 5s by default and change reconciliation to mark synthetic debits with a reconciliation flag so enforcers treat them as idempotent if an identical non-reconciliation debit exists within window. Also add a compact epoch-merge logic: when a shard receives a debit whose epoch is only +1 and a matching request-id already exists in the cache, bump it to a reconciled state instead of double-applying.

Impact of fix: Should eliminate the observed double-debits during handoff without changing normal accounting behavior. Performance impact is minimal (one extra normalization hash and modest TTL increase).
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a 4-shard route with autoscaling enabled and route aliasing (alias A -> canonical route R).
2) Generate steady traffic with a request-id header present (use the load generator that includes X-Request-Id).
3) Trigger a rebalance by scaling shards down/up (simulate lease handoff).
4) Observe per-route meter dashboard: look for 1-3s spikes where token consumption temporarily doubles for route R.
5) Verify by correlating request-ids present in the router logs and the two debit events (old epoch, new epoch) in metering logs.
acceptance_criteria: No double-debit spikes reproducible in synthetic handoff test (load test with controlled handoffs) for 1000 sequential requests.
Deduped meter stream shows single debit per request-id across epoch transitions in staging for 48 hours.
No measurable latency regression (>1ms p95) on the hot path for normalized requests.
New unit + integration tests added covering shard handoff with normalization-first flow.
Release notes updated documenting behavior change to reconciliation emissions.
qa_steps: Run integration scenario in qa-cluster: deploy a route with aliasing and run the handoff script from tools/handoff-sim.sh (see PR docs).
Verify dedupe cache entries using admin endpoint /admin/dedupe/inspect?key=<route>-<request-id> immediately after handoff.
Compare downstream billing aggregation for the test route before and after fix; expect 0% difference for the controlled test window.
Run a 24h soak on staging with randomized handoff timings and assert no >0.5% unexplained variance between realtime meter counts and aggregation pipeline.
rollback_plan: If the fix causes regressions, revert the PR and re-enable the synthetic debit suppression toggle (feature-flagged). Monitor the billing discrepancy dashboard; if errors remain >1% re-open emergency rollback and route traffic to a safe fallback model (read-only accounting path).
